result.topic: PAN-OS/Panorama target= proxy scope (op/config/log/REST) and Panorama log-aggregation defaults

confirmedFacts.claim: Panorama's XML API accepts target=<firewall-serial> to proxy type=op operational commands to a specific managed firewall.
confirmedFacts.evidence: curl -X POST 'https://<panorama>/api?&type=op&cmd=<show><system><info></info></system></show>&target=<device-serial-number>' -- worked example, same shown on 10-1 version of the page too.

confirmedFacts.claim: type=config&action=get with target=<serial> is a real, working combination (proxies candidate-config get through Panorama to a firewall).

The config get/show target-application logic in the pan-python XML API client is action-agnostic: a single shared __type_config() internal method appends target=self.serial identically for show, get, delete, set, edit, move, rename, clone, override, and multi-config -- there is no code path that special-cases 'get' vs 'show' for target handling.
confirmedFacts.evidence: def show(...): self.__type_config('show', query, extra_qs) / def get(...): self.__type_config('get', query, extra_qs) / def __type_config(self, action, query, extra_qs=None): ... if self.serial is not None: query['target'] = self.serial

confirmedFacts.claim: The official Palo Alto Networks Python SDK (pan-os-python, successor to pandevice) is built directly on top of pan-python's pan.xapi.PanXapi class (imports it, and its PanDevice.XapiWrapper reflectively mirrors every public PanXapi method including log()). A Firewall object attached under a Panorama object gets its xapi constructed with serial=<its serial> so that ALL proxied calls -- op, config get/show, commit, export, report, user-id -- carry target=<serial> automatically.
confirmedFacts.evidence: def generate_xapi(self): ... if self.serial is not None and self.hostname is None: ... kwargs = {'pan_device': self, 'api_key': self.panorama().api_key, 'hostname': self.panorama().hostname, ..., 'serial': self.serial} -- comment: "Connect to this firewall via Panorama with 'target' argument set to this firewall's serial number."

confirmedFacts.claim: pan-python's log() method (used for type=log submit and the action=get job-poll) never references self.serial and never adds a target query key -- unlike every other request-type method in the same file, which all explicitly do query['target'] = self.serial. Since pan-os-python inherits this method unmodified via reflection, this gap propagates into the official SDK too.
confirmedFacts.evidence: def log(self, log_type=None, nlogs=None, skip=None, filter=None, interval=None, timeout=None, extra_qs=None): ... query = {}; query['type'] = 'log'; query['key'] = self.api_key; ... [no self.serial / target anywhere in this method, in either the submit query or the action=get job-poll query]

confirmedFacts.claim: Palo Alto Networks' own Cortex XSOAR PAN-OS/Panorama integration (published on the pan.dev developer portal) states explicitly and verbatim that target only works for operational commands and is NOT usable for log retrieval (or commit, or PCAP).
confirmedFacts.evidence: "The target argument is supported only in operational type commands. Meaning, you cannot use it with commit, logs, or PCAP commands." (verbatim, also present at github.com/demisto/content/blob/master/Packs/PAN-OS/Integrations/Panorama/README.md line 55)

confirmedFacts.claim: Official docs.paloaltonetworks.com Retrieve Logs (API) pages document no target parameter at all -- neither confirming nor denying it -- listing only log-type, query, nlogs, skip, dir, action, and job-id as parameters.
confirmedFacts.evidence: Documented parameters for log retrieval limited to: log-type, query, nlogs, skip, dir, action, job-id. No mention of target anywhere on the page.

confirmedFacts.claim: REST API query parameters are documented separately for Firewall vs Panorama endpoints, and target is not among them for either; Panorama's REST location values are documented as only 'shared' and 'device-group' -- 'panorama-pushed' is a firewall-only location value.
confirmedFacts.evidence: Firewall location values: predefined | shared (Objects only) | vsys | panorama-pushed. Panorama location values: shared | device-group. Documented query parameters overall: name, location, vsys, device-group, input-format, output-format, newname, where, dst -- no 'target'.

confirmedFacts.claim: The official pan-os-python SDK contains zero REST API client code -- it is entirely XML-API-based (built on pan.xapi.PanXapi) -- meaning there is no official-SDK precedent for a target=/serial-based REST proxy mechanism either.
confirmedFacts.evidence: grep for 'restapi|rest_api|REST' across base.py returns zero references to any REST client/session code; `import pan.xapi` is the sole API transport used throughout.

confirmedFacts.claim: Each managed firewall stores its traffic/threat/URL logs locally by default and does NOT automatically send them to Panorama; achieving centralized visibility on Panorama requires forwarding all firewall logs to Panorama explicitly.
confirmedFacts.evidence: "Each firewall stores its log files locally by default and cannot display the logs that reside on other firewalls." ... to achieve global visibility "you must forward all firewall logs to Panorama."

confirmedFacts.claim: The explicit configuration Suncoast's firewalls need for Panorama log aggregation is: (1) create a Log Forwarding profile defining destinations for Traffic/Threat/WildFire/URL Filtering/Data Filtering/Tunnel/Authentication logs, then (2) assign that profile to Security (and Authentication/DoS Protection) policy rules and network zones -- this is not a default/automatic state.
confirmedFacts.evidence: "Create a Log Forwarding profile. The profile defines the destinations for Traffic, Threat, WildFire Submission, URL Filtering, Data Filtering, Tunnel and Authentication logs." / "Assign the Log Forwarding profile to policy rules and network zones. Security, Authentication, and DoS Protection rules support log forwarding."

remainingGaps: No docs.paloaltonetworks.com page (Retrieve Logs API, XML API request types, or Panorama API use-cases) states in an explicit prose sentence, either way, whether target= is honored for type=log -- the page is simply silent on the parameter. The 'confirmed does NOT work' conclusion rests on convergent SDK-source-code + Cortex-XSOAR-integration-doc evidence, not a direct official-docs statement -- still needs a live Panorama test (submit a type=log&target=<serial> job and check whether the returned entries actually reflect that firewall's logs vs. Panorama's own view, or whether it errors/silently ignores target) to fully close this.

No official docs worked example shows type=config&action=show combined with target= specifically (only action=get has a worked third-party example). The pan-python SDK evidence treats show/get identically, but this has not been seen in an official docs page or a live device test.

Whether the PAN-OS server-side API handler itself silently ignores an unrecognized target= param on a REST call (returning Panorama's own object, no error) or rejects it (error) is untested -- no source, official or community, shows anyone having tried target= against a REST endpoint at all. Needs a live test against Suncoast's Panorama.

Whether Suncoast's actual managed firewalls have Log Forwarding profiles configured pointing at Panorama/a Collector Group is a live-environment/config-review question, not resolvable from public docs -- this determines whether querying Panorama's own hostname directly (no target, no proxy) for type=log would return anything for those 8 Azure firewalls at all.

No official doc or SDK source addresses whether target= works with type=log differently on Panorama Panorama-mode vs Management-Only-mode, or whether firewalls' own local logs (if forwarding is NOT configured) can be reached in any way other than connecting directly to that firewall's own management hostname.

recommendedCodeChanges.change: Section 6 (Panorama Proxying & Log Aggregation): upgrade the 'Open gap' bullet on type=log+target from 'not stated either way' to a stronger, still-labeled-unconfirmed-but-evidenced claim: cite the Cortex XSOAR/pan.dev integration doc's explicit statement ('target argument is supported only in operational type commands... cannot use it with commit, logs, or PCAP') and the pan-python/pan-os-python SDK source-code gap (log() never sets target, unlike every other request-type method) as convergent community/SDK evidence that target= does NOT work for type=log -- while keeping the live-device test as the final confirmation step. Also add the exact verbatim quote now confirmed for log aggregation defaults: 'Each firewall stores its log files locally by default and cannot display the logs that reside on other firewalls' (docs.paloaltonetworks.com/panorama/administration/manage-log-collection/configure-log-forwarding-to-panorama), plus the two required forwarding-config steps (Log Forwarding profile creation + assignment to rules/zones), and add an explicit new gap: whether Suncoast's 8 Panorama-managed Azure firewalls actually have that forwarding configured is unknown and must be asked/checked.

In _xml_config_get()'s docstring, soften 'action=show combined with target was NOT found with an explicit worked example in official docs -- treat that combination as unconfirmed' to note that community SDK source (pan-python's shared __type_config method, inherited unmodified by the official pan-os-python SDK) applies target identically regardless of action (show/get/set/edit/delete/rename/clone/move/override/multi-config) -- i.e. medium-confidence SDK-level corroboration exists even though no official-docs worked example for show+target specifically was found. No functional code change needed; the existing target passthrough is already correct for both actions.

No functional bug found -- the current design already avoids passing target= to any type=log call (get_traffic_logs/get_url_filtering_logs/get_dns_threat_logs take no target param, and _collect_panorama_managed_firewall in main.py only uses target= for the type=op license call, falling back to requiring a direct 'host' for logs/profiles/rules). This is the correct posture given the research above and should be preserved. Recommend only a docstring/comment update in main.py's _collect_panorama_managed_firewall (around the 'log-query mechanics were not confirmed to work via Panorama's target= proxy' comment) to cite the stronger convergent evidence now found (XSOAR doc + pan-python/pan-os-python source) rather than leaving it as a bare unconfirmed statement, and to add a note that even direct-to-firewall log queries will return nothing meaningful for logs that were never forwarded anywhere -- that's orthogonal to target= and governed entirely by each firewall's own Log Forwarding profile config, which must be confirmed with Suncoast.
